issue.goal: Idle 15m / absolute 8h Session timeouts, failed login ends carried Session, end-all-Sessions for an Account, session-end audit, restart survival

findings.violation: KB unavailable. spring.session.timeout=${app.session.absolute-timeout} applies to every Spring Session, including Visitor (CSRF-only) Sessions that any unauthenticated GET /api/csrf creates. Their rows now live 8h instead of the previous 30m default: 16x more unauthenticated rows an anonymous caller can pile up in spring_session before any rate limit exists.
findings.proposed: Leave spring.session.timeout at a short default (for example the idle timeout) and in SessionControl.start() call session.setMaxInactiveInterval(properties.absoluteTimeout()) so only authenticated Sessions keep their row for the absolute limit (JDBC stores MAX_INACTIVE_INTERVAL per row). Add a test that a Visitor Session's max inactive interval stays short and an authenticated one is the absolute timeout.

findings.violation: KB unavailable. endAll is a public API claimed as covering acceptance criterion 3, but no test exercises it. Its two branches (the request's own Session via end(), other Sessions via deleteById) and its per-Session audit loop are not shared with endOldestBeyondLimit, so later issues 08/09/11-15 would inherit untested behaviour.
findings.proposed: Add a @SpringBootTest that logs in over MockMvc, then calls the SessionControl bean's endAll(accountId, reason, request, response) with (a) a request carrying that Session and (b) a request without it; assert /api/me returns 401 afterwards and one session-end event per ended Session with the given reason and user.id.

findings.violation: KB unavailable. Acceptance criterion 4 says each Session that expires emits session-end. A Session is audited only when it is presented again after its limit or ended by a new login. A Session that is abandoned is deleted silently by Spring Session JDBC cleanup (JDBC fires no expiry events), with no session-end event. Also, an abandoned Session later removed by a new login is audited as new_login although it had already passed its idle limit.
findings.proposed: Human decision: accept presentation-time auditing (document it in the issue), or add a scheduled sweep that audits and deletes authenticated Sessions past their limits before Spring Session cleanup, or at least compute the real reason (idle/absolute) when endOldestBeyondLimit/endAll remove an already-expired Session.

decisions.kb_finding: Abandoned expired Sessions are deleted by Spring Session JDBC cleanup with no session-end event; already-expired Sessions removed by a later login are recorded as new_login.
decisions.chosen_action: Do not follow KB recommendation: no KB available; chose option C + A. endOldestBeyondLimit and endAll record idle_timeout/absolute_timeout when the removed Session had already expired; the remaining gap for untouched abandoned Sessions is accepted and noted in the issue. No scheduled sweep.
decisions.reuse: Audit-completeness questions for records a store expires in the background: record the true reason wherever the app touches them and document the untouched-expiry gap.
